full_judgment:
11. In the instant ease, the name of the returned candidate was published on 19.2.1977 and the petition was filed on 21.3.1977. It is submitted by Mr. Aminul Huq that the Election Laws are to be construed strictly. There appears to be substance in this submission of Mr. Aminul Huq the period of limitation for filing election petition is 30 days from the date of publication of the name of the returned candidate in the official gazette. The amendment was prayed for about 2-1 years after the period of limitation: for filing the election petition was over. 

 13. Relying on these rules Mr. Asrarul Hossain the learned Advocate submitted that at any stage of the hearing of the election petition, the Tribunal may allow amendment of the petition. In this connection he has referred to Order 6, Rule 17 C.P.C. There is no doubt that an amendment which would not change the nature and character of the suit may be allowed at any stage of the hearing of the suit and there are instances that amendments were allowed even at the Appellate stage. In the instant case, obviously, the period of limitation for filing the election petition was over about 2½ years before the amendment was prayed and allowed. The amendment allowed caused a fundamental change in the nature and character of the election petition. In. the original election petition there was no allegation that there was any irregularity or illegality in the counting of ballot papers. The election laws are to be construed strictly. Taking this aspect into consideration the amendment allowed by the Tribunal on 22.8.1979 appears to be not proper. 

 16. In the instant case there was no prayer made in the original election petition for recounting of votes. There was no allegation that ballot papers were counted in insufficient light and there was no proper counting of ballot papers. The amendment was prayed for after about 21 years after expiry of the period of limitation. The petitioner gave a go bye to all the allegations made in the original election petition. He made out an entirely new case in the application for amendment filed on 22.8.79 the allegations were primarily directed against the Presiding Officers of the Polling Stations. No allegation was made against the public servants concerned in the original petition. The petitioner did not have the opportunity to cross-examine respondent No. 2. Whatever foundation for recounting was laid by the evidence of respondent No. 2 might have been demolished by the petitioner in cross-examination. Be that as it may, the denial of cross-examination of respondent No. 2 to the petitioner without any reasonable cause was a violation of the principle of natural justice and Rule 50 (2) of the Union Paris had Election Rules, 1916. In the circumstances, the Tribunal was not legally entitled to recount the ballot papers.
